She won 1st runner up place in the competition. It is being held to build comradery and continue collaborating with American schools across the Kingdom of Morocco.

The spelling bee was held at the Moroccan American Legation of Tangier. Yassmin has been doing Anglia Exams for the past 2 years and is working on her level C-1 Proficiency level currently.

American Group International and Anglia Morocco is very grateful for the opportunity to showcase our talent and we thank the American School in Tangier for inviting us. We would personally like to thank Francesca Ghi, coordinator of the event and Michael Prada, Principal of the American School of Tangier.

American Group International (AGI) is proud to announce that as of Spring 2026, the organization is officially recognized as a partner of the American School Counselor Association (ASCA) in the United States through its Principal and Founder, Julie Wilburn.

The American School Counselor Association (ASCA), founded in 1952, is the leading professional organization for school counselors in the U.S. ASCA sets the standard for student counseling programs by providing ethical guidelines, professional development, research, and a nationally recognized framework known as the ASCA National Model. Through this partnership, AGI strengthens its mission to provide professional, research-based guidance and counseling support to students in Morocco and internationally. This affiliation ensures that AGI’s services align with recognized U.S. standards in academic advising, student support, and college readiness planning.

## American High School – Yass Prize Awardee

# Celebrating Excellence with Our Partner

## American High School – Yass Prize Awardee

At **American Group International (AGI)**, we take immense pride in celebrating the outstanding achievements of our partner, **American High School (AHS)**. Their recognition as a distinguished **Yass Prize Awardee** reflects their visionary leadership, innovative educational model, and unwavering commitment to empowering learners across diverse communities.

This milestone is more than an award — it is a testament to AHS’s transformative impact and the shared mission we proudly uphold together: expanding access, opportunity, and excellence in education.

### What Makes This Achievement Exceptional

- **Educational Innovation:** AHS is redefining modern learning with flexible, student‑centered pathways.
- **Impactful Reach:** Their programs uplift underserved, marginalized, and justice‑involved learners.
- **Leadership in Equity:** AHS sets a national standard for inclusive, high‑quality education.
- **Shared Vision:** AGI is honored to partner with an institution that aligns with our mission of global educational advancement.

Join us in congratulating American High School on this remarkable accomplishment.

 [Learn More About Their Achievement](https://yassprize.org/awardees/american-high-school)

## American High School – Yass Prize (Embedded)

View the original American High School page from the Yass Prize website directly below:

If the embedded page does not display,  [click here to open it in a new tab.](https://yassprize.org/awardees/american-high-school)

## About American High School

American High School is an innovative education network founded in 2004. It supports incarcerated, marginalized, and justice‑involved learners by offering accredited high school diplomas and career‑focused certifications. Programs operate in juvenile detention centers, reentry initiatives, and underserved communities, helping students reconnect with education and build stronger futures.

Through trauma‑informed teaching, flexible scheduling, and individualized pathways, American High School works to remove barriers to learning. Students gain both academic credentials and practical skills that prepare them for employment, additional training, or further education, creating real opportunities for long‑term success.

### Key focus areas

- **Accredited diplomas:** High school completion for students who have been pushed out of traditional systems.
- **Career certifications:** Training that connects learners to real job opportunities and trades.
- **Justice‑involved youth:** Programs tailored for incarcerated and reentering students.
- **Trauma‑informed approach:** Educators trained to support students with complex life experiences.
- **Flexible learning:** Schedules and pathways that adapt to students’ realities.

## 

## **Chichester College Group International**

## **(CCGi) – Overview**

### **A Leader in International Education**

CCGi is the international arm of Chichester College Group (CCG), which has been rated 'Outstanding' by Ofsted, the UK’s education standards authority.

The group comprises seven colleges across ten campuses across West Sussex and Brighton & Hove.

Mission & Reputation

### CCGi’s mission: “Changing lives through learning.”.

Recognized for academic excellence and comprehensive student support—especially for international learners.

### **Key Programs Offered**

English Language Courses: General English (15 & 21), delivered via the British Council-accredited Chichester English Language School, ranked among the top 5% in the UK.

A-Levels & AS-Levels: Two-year A-Levels at Chichester and Worthing; one-year AS-Levels at Worthing.

Vocational Courses & BTECs: Practical, skills-focused courses in areas like hospitality, engineering, health & social care, creative arts.

University Foundation Programs: Pathways ensuring progression to UK or international universities.

Higher Education Degrees: Undergraduate degrees (HNC, HND, level 4–6) in fields like business, engineering, art, media, motorsport, animal management, music, sports, teaching—accredited by institutions such as University of the Arts London (UAL) and University of Brighton.

Study Abroad, Winter/Summer Schools: Short-term immersive experiences combining academics with British cultural activities.

### **Student Support & Unique Experience**

Comprehensive services: Visa guidance, accommodation assistance (homestays, halls), welfare, enrichment and social activities.

Highly equipped campuses: State-of-the-art facilities including farms, animal care centres, equine training, workshops, labs, and creative arts studios.

Cultural immersion: Organized trips to iconic UK sites like London, Oxford, Stonehenge, fostering personal growth and global citizenship.

Global student body: Enrols students from regions including East Asia, Europe, and beyond.

### **Strategic Partnerships & Agents Network**

CCGi maintains partnerships with academic institutions, awarding bodies, and global agents who represent them locally to prospective students.

Strategic collaborations include organisations like NOCN, supporting qualification accreditation.

#### Spotlight on CCGi Colleges

1. Chichester College

Main campus in Chichester, plus Brinsbury (agricultural campus with a working farm and animal care facilities) .

Offers A-Levels, BTECs, vocational programs, and some university-level courses.

2. Northbrook College

Based in Worthing with campuses in West Durrington and Shoreham-by-Sea (campus sale planned in 2025) .

Strong in creative and cultural higher education: fashion, photography, media (validated by UAL), plus motorsport engineering (via University of Brighton) .

3. Worthing College

Sixth-form college in Worthing offering A-Levels & AS-Levels; also, part of CCG’s broader vocational and international portfolio.

4. Brighton MET College

Former Brighton MET (merged August 2021); campuses in central and east Brighton.

Offers trades, technical subjects, adult education, and visual arts progression.

5. Crawley College and Haywards Heath College

Additional FE/Higher Education providers under the CCG umbrella—extending geographic range and offerings.

6. Brinsbury

Specialized land-based and agricultural centre; integral to Chichester College’s offerings.

American Group International is a proud partner of CCGi and we will be working on projects and educational programs to help the local Moroccan community.

records.body_markdown:
HISTORY OF SOI

### ***American Group International has partnered with Energia SOI to bring one of the best cognitive programs for children and young adults.  Programs are customized for students with Reading and Math difficulties.***

### ***[Learning Math (Funny)](http://www.americangroup-international.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Learning-Math-Funny.wmv)***

[video width="1280" height="720" mp4="http://www.americangroup-international.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/ENERGIA-SOI-INTRODUCTION-02112016.mp4"][/video]

### "EDUCATION IS NOT THE LEARNING OF FACTS, BUT THE TRAINING OF THE MIND TO THINK"

##### -ALBERT EINSTEIN

Dr. J.P. Guilford was an American Psychologist best remembered for his psychometric study of human intelligence, including the distinction between convergent and divergent production. A Review of General Psychology survey, published in 2002, ranked Guilford as the 27th most cited psychologist of the 20th century.  
  
Our story starts back during World War II when about 35% of pilots were failing out of the Air Corps. These men had IQs over 120, but they still weren’t making it.  
It became Dr. J.P. Guilford’s job to find a new way of measuring intelligence. Guilford drew up sets of intellectual functions required for the various Army Corps jobs and constructed tests that measured those abilities.  
  
Guildford’s tests were used to select personnel with the most intellectual potential for training, and the washout rate dropped by more than 25 percent!  
Pleased with Guilford’s great success, the Defense Department-funded Guilford for the next twenty years in the Aptitudes Project at the University of Southern California.  
  
He and his students continued to identify many different abilities, and a model began to take shape. That model became the Structure of Intellect.  
  
Our founder, Dr. Mary Meeker, was one of Guilford’s students. She saw the potential of the model, especially for identifying learning difficulties. Dr. Meeker soon discovered that certain intellectual abilities were related to basic learning: reading, arithmetic, higher math, creativity, and more.  
  
Dr. Meeker’s most exciting and important contribution was her realization that intellectual abilities could be taught! This added a whole new dimension to Guilford’s work.  
  
At this point, not only could abilities be identified, but they could be taught and developed, too! This coupling is what makes SOI unique. It provides the basis of all our tests, products, and programs that have been developed by Dr. Meeker and her husband, Dr. Robert Meeker.  
  
SOI Systems was officially founded in 1965. And here we are today, more than 50 years later, continuing to impact lives and make a difference, all thanks to the research and development of such a powerful learning system!

records.body_markdown:
## **What is an online/virtual classroom???**

![](http://www.americangroup-international.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/cfd86ae1-0a30-40d0-9d7b-3d5bf182bef6-1024x682.jpg)

A virtual classroom is a digital replica of a traditional classroom or training room. The instructors teach, and the participants learn in real-time, face-to-face but via internet-enabled technology devices. The classroom or the meeting room staple – whiteboard – remains intact. Brainstorming, idealization, and discussions happen in real-time. Tests are given and taken pre and post the session. The reports are ready right after the session is over.

Everything remains the way it is. The only difference is: an online classroom uses technology to support instruction and learning. What are the advantages of a virtual classroom? It offers more flexibility over a traditional classroom. You can deliver the instruction to a geographically dispersed audience at one time. Both the instructors and learners have rich experience of collaborating with other learners and instructors from around the world. The attendance is automatically tracked. Moreover, online collaboration typically incorporates more communication tools, such as chat, open discussion boards, polls, multimedia content, and social media.

The **online class software** works in a similar fashion for businesses. You can train employees, vendors, partners, and customers face-to-face in real-time via a standalone app or you can also integrate it with your website, CMS, ERP, or LMS. You can conduct the training even when the stakeholders are on the move. They can access the e-Learning material and attend the live session from their smartphones, tablets, or laptops.

Teacher Training Program Assistant:
Work under a teacher’s supervision to give students additional attention and instruction.
Duties
Teacher assistants typically do the following:

Reinforce lessons presented by teachers by reviewing material with students one-on-one or in small groups
Enforce school and class rules to help teach students proper behavior
Help teachers with record keeping, such as tracking attendance and calculating grades
Help teachers prepare for lessons by getting materials ready or setting up equipment, such as computers
Help supervise students in class, between classes, during lunch and recess, and on field trips
Teacher assistants also are called teacher aides, instructional aides, paraprofessionals, education assistants and para-educators.
Generally, teachers introduce new material to students, and teacher assistants help reinforce the lessons by working with individual students or small groups of students. For example, after the teacher presents a lesson, a teacher assistant may help a small group of students as they try to master the material.
Teachers may seek feedback from assistants to monitor students’ progress. Some teachers and teacher assistants meet regularly to discuss lesson plans and student development. Teacher assistants sometimes help teachers by grading tests and checking homework.
Some teacher assistants work only with special education students. These students often attend regular classes, and teacher assistants help them understand the material and adapt the information to their learning style.
With students who have more severe disabilities, assistants may work with them in separate classes. Teacher assistants help these students with basic needs, such as eating or personal hygiene. With young adults, they may help students with disabilities learn skills necessary for them to find a job or live independently after graduation.
Some teacher assistants work in specific locations in the school. For example, some work in computer laboratories, teaching students how to use computers and helping them use software. Others work as recess or lunchroom attendants, supervising students during these times of the day.
Although most teacher assistants work in elementary, middle, and high schools, others work in preschools and childcare centers. Often, one or two assistants work with a lead teacher to provide the individual attention that young children need. They help with educational activities. They also supervise the children at play and help with feeding and other basic care.

Anglia Mastery Qualification Awarded UCAS Tariff Points - Anglia Morocco
Successful candidates can now gain tariff points for UCAS applications from the Anglia Examinations Mastery level.
As of May 2021, students successfully completing the AIM Qualifications Level 3 Certificate in ESOL International (Anglia Mastery)
, will be awarded tariff points which can count towards their university application.
See the Anglia Exam UCAS tariif points allocation for the Mastery Level below
#### Caculating your UCAS Tariff Points for the Anglia Mastery Exam
From May 2021 the tariff points allocated by UCAS are as follows:
Level Attained
UCAS Tariff Points
Pass (P)
16 Points
Merit (M)
20 Points
Distinction (D)
24 Points
### UCAS Tariff Points Calculator
You can check your tariff point allocation on the UCAS site. Simply type the word “Anglia” into the box entitled “My Qualifications” and enter either “P”, “D” or “M” depending on whether your achieved a pass, merit or distinction.
This is tremendous news! All those thousands of students who have sat Anglia Exams around the world and who have progressed through our Step-by-Step programme, can now aim for our Mastery Exam, knowing that it will help with their university applications in the UK.
“This really is a game-changer for anyone looking to go to a UK university,” said Andy Coxon from AIM Qualifications and Assessment Group. “Now, as well as getting a certificate from an Ofqual accredited awarding organisation, learners have the added benefit of using the qualification as part of their tariff total for university .”
AIM Qualifications partnered with Anglia Examinations to develop this unique ESOL International Qualification.
“UCAS recognition of the Anglia Mastery exam is a tremendous milestone for Anglia exam takers all over the world. Many of our students have grown up with Anglia, starting with our First Step or Junior exams as young children and progressing through the levels using our Step-by-Step approach. The fact that our highest level now provides points towards university applications means that Anglia Exam takers have a clearer learning destination to aim for as they master the English language.”
Steve Bannister Group Director- Anglia Examinations.
Centres wishing to offer this qualification must be an AIM Qualifications recognised centre. Check out our information page on the Anglia ESOL Mastery Exam for more information.

records.title: “Julie Our newest franchisee from Morocco” an article published in the Anglia November Newsletter 2021
records.body_text:
“Julie Our newest franchisee from Morocco” an article published in the Anglia November Newsletter 2021 - Anglia Morocco
### Introducing Julie A. Wilburn
Julie is our newest franchisee from Morocco:
1. Can you please introduce Anglia Morocco to our partners around the world?
Anglia Morocco under the brand American Group International School (AGI) was formed with my desire to reach the unreached areas in Morocco with the low-cost testing of international exams. The main idea was to set up small centers and freelancing to promote English in the rural areas of Morocco.
I believe if the rural areas were reached we would have many more opportunities open up on the international level for the lower-income citizens. In times past, English was in Morocco something that only families of higher income status could obtain. I was particularly concerned about the southern part of Morocco as the current English franchise providers seem to be more concentrated in the cities. We will of course set up centers in the city, but I want to basically establish regional outreaches in each of the 12 regions in Morocco. Currently, we are working on projects that are forming in 5 regions.
2. Name 2- 3 good reasons why a partnership with Anglia Examinations is good?
As an American living abroad and teaching English as a second language to Moroccans, I have seen that many do not know the differences in American English and British English. I like the idea of having 1. The ability to let students be able to test and take exams with both types and it is considered acceptable. 2. This also lets me give professionals knowledge and confidence in both types of grammar and vocabulary. 3. The certificates do not expire.
3. How has the pandemic impacted the English Language ecosystem? Is the outlook positive?
I think younger Moroccans have for years seen a transformation from the language of French in Morocco. During the pandemic, many Moroccans living abroad had to return home or had to use online learning as they did not have access to school. The majority of the platforms are in English and this has Morocco, as a country discussing seriously what is the best course of studies in the future with many universities requiring that some professions require English. So, now that Anglia offers online exams that platform will expand also reaching remote areas.
4. Random Question – If you could bring something extinct (thing or person) back to life, what would you choose and why?
In all honesty, I would bring Mr. Kolbe my high school English/Literature teacher back to life. He taught me that I was not to focus on just the grammar book to teach people to love English. He taught me that I should actually first show empathy and care to my students. He felt as a teacher that reading and comprehension are the biggest base for learning English. I wish to place in my students the desire to learn English to reach the world in humanity.
